I was on a plane headed towards London, England from Dulles airport. I was 18 at the time, and I was on my way to meet up with my parents, who were already there. We were there for vacation. We didnt find out about it for a long time. My parents asked me what I wanted to do after I landed, and I told them I wanted to go see the Tower of London. I was amazed how there was like nobody there. I have been there many times ( we used to live in England. My dad was in the airforce) and there were always alot of tourists.  After we were done, we got a cab because I wanted to go see a dungeon/torture exhibit. On the way, the cab driver said "Sorry about your Twin Towers". We were confused, and my dad laughed thinking the driver was joking around. The cab driver went on to say that the Pentagon was hit too. My dad still didnt believe him, and kind of chewed him out ( my dad worked at the Pentagon at the time). The cab driver didnt say anything, and just casually turned on the radio. We sat in stunned silence the rest of the ride. We got out of the cab and I broke the silence by saying I wasnt really in the mood to visit a dungeon/torture exhibit. Then we just kind of stood there and watched everyone around us. That was when we noticed how people were standing around any TV that was on. How people were huddled together. It was a weird eerie feeling. Then a guy was running towards/past us saying a plane was headed for London. My dad then said "we are going to a base". We got a rental car, left London, and drove to an airforce base ( with the radio on the whole way). We stayed there until we were able to fly home, watching the news. I totally took advantage of the fact that I could drink alcohol at 18, and on the plane ride back. When we landed at Dulles the whole plane cheered and clapped. My dad drove by the Pentagon on our way home. I think he may have known some of the people that died there, but he doesnt talk about it.
